documents.title: Lump in my neck
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I noticed a couple of lumps on the side of my neck, not sore. Also in my groin I think. I've been more tired again and get full fast when I eat. My blood doctor appointment is Feb 24. Should I come in before that?

documents.title: RE: Lump in my neck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. I sent a note to your hematology team so they know before your visit, and they agreed to keep the 2/24 appointment and see you then. If you develop fevers, drenching night sweats, trouble swallowing or breathing, or the lumps grow quickly, call us or them right away and we will see you sooner.

reports.text:
LYMPH NODE, LEFT CERVICAL, ULTRASOUND-GUIDED CORE NEEDLE BIOPSY
Microscopic: lymph node architecture effaced by crowded, back-to-back neoplastic follicles. The follicles are composed of a uniform population of small cleaved lymphocytes (centrocytes); large cells are infrequent.

Cytogenetics/FISH: t(14;18)(q32;q21) IGH-BCL2 rearrangement detected.

documents.title: Hematology-Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY-ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 02/24/2023

Mr. Dunn is 58 and returns on scheduled surveillance for hairy cell leukemia, in remission since cladribine in March 2022. Over the past several months his tiredness has crept back and is worse. He fills up quickly at meals. He has felt painless swellings in his neck and groin. Night sweats now and then. Weight down 4 kg (9 lb) over this period, today 69.5 kg. No fever, cough, chest pain or infections lately.

Medications: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: alcohol use disorder in sustained remission, no alcohol since February 2021. Former smoker, 30 pack-years.

Exam: several firm, nontender lymph nodes in both cervical chains and both inguinal regions. Spleen mildly enlarged. No hepatomegaly.

Labs: hemoglobin 11.6, MCV 90 (mild normocytic anemia); WBC 5.6, platelets 163, no hairy cells. LDH 340 U/L (reference up to 245), elevated. Albumin 3.4.

Procedure: ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a left cervical node performed today.
Pathology (final 03/01/2023): crowded, back-to-back follicles of uniform small cleaved lymphocytes; CD10 and BCL2 positive; t(14;18) detected.

Assessment:
1. Follicular lymphoma, newly diagnosed, with constitutional symptoms and enlarging nodes that warrant treatment.
2. Hairy cell leukemia, remains in remission.

Plan:
- Staging PET-CT and hepatitis B serologies before anti-CD20 therapy.
- Intend bendamustine and rituximab for 6 cycles if staging confirms.
- We will see him again after PET-CT.

Hematology-Oncology

documents.title: PET-CT Skull Base to Mid-Thigh — Staging
documents.author: nuclear medicine
documents.body:
FDG PET-CT, SKULL BASE TO MID-THIGH
Indication: newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma, staging.
Fasting glucose at injection acceptable for imaging.
Findings:
- Neck: multiple FDG-avid lymph nodes in bilateral cervical chains.
- Chest: no FDG-avid mediastinal, hilar or axillary nodes. Lungs: stable 4 mm right upper lobe nodule without uptake.
- Abdomen/pelvis: multiple FDG-avid bilateral inguinal lymph nodes. Spleen mildly enlarged with physiologic uptake. No retroperitoneal or mesenteric adenopathy. Liver without focal lesion; no ascites. Pancreas atrophic with calcifications, unchanged in appearance from CT 2021.
- Bones: no focal marrow uptake.
Impression: FDG-avid lymphoma in cervical and inguinal nodes; mild splenomegaly. No other sites of disease.

Mr. Dunn completed 6 cycles of bendamustine and rituximab for follicular lymphoma (March-August 2023). End-of-treatment PET-CT 09/20/2023 shows a complete metabolic response. He feels better, nodes are no longer palpable and his appetite is back.

Ondansetron no longer needed.

orders.reason: Progressive dysphagia to solids then liquids with weight loss

documents.title: Acute Visit — Trouble Swallowing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Swallowing trouble for 3 months, getting worse. Started with meat and bread sticking, now soft food and sometimes liquids. Food feels like it stops behind the breastbone after eating; occasionally brings food back up undigested. No pain with swallowing. No vomiting blood, no black stools. Weight down noticeably; pants falling off. Appetite fine but cannot get food down.
No fevers, sweats or lumps. Sober three years this month.

Exam: BP 126/75, HR 67, T 36.6, SpO2 98%, Wt 63.6 kg (67.4 kg in October), BMI 20.2.
Thin, temporal wasting. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. No palpable inguinal nodes. Spleen not palpable. Abdomen soft, nontender. Spider angiomas on chest. No edema.

A/P:
1. Progressive dysphagia, solids then liquids, with weight loss, in a former 30 pack-year smoker with heavy alcohol history: needs urgent evaluation for an obstructing esophageal lesion. Urgent GI referral placed and called.
2. Weight loss: soft and liquid high-calorie foods in the meantime; take Creon with each.
3. Type 3c diabetes: risk of lows with reduced intake. Check before meals; call for any reading under 80. Glargine 24 units for now.
4. Labs: CBC, CMP, A1c.

documents.title: Lab review

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation — Dysphagia
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 02/21/2024

HPI: 59-year-old man known to our clinic for chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency (2021), also with treated hairy cell leukemia and follicular lymphoma. For three months swallowing has become steadily harder, first for solids and now for liquids. He has lost 10 lb without changing his diet or activity. He sometimes regurgitates undigested food, and after meals feels food lodged behind the sternum.

Meds: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, 30 pack-years. Alcohol use disorder, abstinent since February 2021.

Exam: cachectic. No lymphadenopathy. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses or organomegaly.
Labs: hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL.

Barium esophagram (today): irregular narrowing of the distal esophagus.

Assessment: progressive dysphagia with an irregular distal esophageal stricture on barium study, highly suspicious for esophageal carcinoma.

Plan: upper endoscopy with biopsy, scheduled 03/05/2024. Continue soft and liquid diet with Creon.

Gastroenterology

conditions.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of lower third of esophagus

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ESOPHAGOGASTRODUODENOSCOPY WITH BIOPSY
Indication: progressive dysphagia, distal esophageal narrowing on barium study.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Findings:
- Esophagus: a friable, partly circumferential mass narrowing the distal esophagus from 35 to 38 cm from the incisors; the standard scope passed with gentle pressure. Multiple biopsies taken. No esophageal varices.
- Stomach: normal; no gastric varices.
- Duodenum: normal to the second portion.
Impression: distal esophageal mass causing narrowing, biopsied. No varices.
Pathology (03/08/2024): squamous cell carcinoma.
Plan: refer to oncology for staging; PET-CT ordered.

documents.title: Call about biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Mike after receiving the pathology: squamous cell cancer of the lower esophagus. GI had already told him by phone. He is frightened but practical; wanted to know whether this means surgery. Explained staging comes first (PET-CT 3/14) and then oncology and surgery will advise. Discussed nutrition: liquid supplements between meals, Creon with each. Watch sugars with low intake. Offered to see him any time; he will call after the oncology visit.

documents.title: PET-CT Skull Base to Mid-Thigh — Esophageal Cancer Staging
documents.author: nuclear medicine
documents.body:
FDG PET-CT, SKULL BASE TO MID-THIGH
Indication: newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma of the distal esophagus. History of follicular lymphoma with complete response 2023.
Comparison: PET-CT 09/20/2023.
Findings:
- Intense FDG uptake in the distal esophageal primary mass.
- No FDG-avid regional or distant lymph nodes. Previously treated cervical and inguinal nodal stations remain without uptake.
- No hepatic, adrenal, pulmonary or osseous metastases. Liver without focal lesion; no ascites. Spleen normal in size.
- Pancreas atrophic with calcifications, unchanged.
Impression: FDG-avid distal esophageal primary without nodal or distant disease.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Plan Letter
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

We met with Mr. Dunn on 03/22/2024 at the multidisciplinary thoracic oncology clinic about his distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. PET-CT shows the primary only, with no nodal or distant disease.

Thoracic surgery reviewed his case. Because of his hepatic dysfunction from chronic hepatitis C, esophagectomy is not being offered.

Recommendation: definitive chemoradiation. Weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel with concurrent radiation to 50.4 Gy, planned to begin 04/08/2024. Baseline ECG normal (PR 170 ms). Ondansetron as needed for nausea during treatment. Dietitian involved for oral nutrition.

We will share treatment summaries with you.

Hematology-Oncology
